message.content:
**Compounded Interest Calculation**

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Principal \(P\) | \$10 000 |
| Annual nominal rate (\(r\)) | 5 % → 0.05 |
| Compounding frequency | **Annually** (default assumption when unspecified) |
| Time \((t)\) | 3 years |

---

### Future Value After 3 Years  
Using the standard compound‑interest formula with annual compounding (\(n = 1\)):
\[
A = P\,\bigl(1+\frac{r}{n}\bigr)^{nt}
   = 10\,000 \times (1+0.05)^{3}
   = 10\,000 \times 1.157625
   \approx \$11\,576.25
\]

### Compound Interest Earned  
Interest accrued over the period:
\[
I_{\text{compound}} = A - P 
                     = 11\,576.25 - 10\,000 
                     = \$1\,576.25
\]

So, at an annual rate of 5%, compounded once per year, you would earn approximately **\$1,576.25** in interest on a \$10,000 investment over three years, bringing your total balance to about **\$11,576.25**.
